summary: Iteration 18 — Backend-only validation of the GBP scope-insufficient fix (403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT). 17/17 pytest passing. Endpoints (/api/gbp/status, /api/gbp/login, /api/gbp/disconnect) return the correct new fields (granted_scopes, scope_ok, accounts_check_status). Static code review of gbp_callback + gbp_list_locations confirmed the spec (scope enforcement, accounts.list probe, differentiated 403 messages, French actionable text, no token logging). Mocked httpx unit tests verify gbp_list_locations 403 branches. Regressions (meta/status, drafts) unaffected. One in-scope bug found & fixed: NameError on `logger` in routes_social.py.

minor.issue: FIXED IN THIS ITERATION. `logger.warning(...)` was called in the accounts_check failure branch but `logger` was never imported → NameError raised whenever accounts.list returned non-200 during OAuth callback (the very failure path the fix was written to handle). Added `import logging` + `logger = logging.getLogger('routes_social')`. Verified module still imports and endpoints respond 200.
Endpoint not present in this build — test accepts 404. If LinkedIn publishing is planned, add the status route symmetric to meta/gbp.

static_review_notes: SocialPublishPanel.jsx: reconnect button correctly rendered when `gbp.connected && gbp.scope_ok === false` with data-testid='social-reconnect-gbp-button' (L215-222). It calls POST /gbp/disconnect (errors swallowed intentionally with /* ignore */) then triggers /gbp/login which redirects to the Google authorization URL. Amber styling + explicit 'Reconnecter (permission manquante)' label + title tooltip are all present. Behaviour matches spec — no changes required.

action_items: None blocking — fix is behaviourally correct end-to-end. Main agent should confirm the logger import fix is acceptable (in-scope test-agent change).
Optional: consider logging accounts_check failures at info level (not warning) since the /drafts?gbp=connected_quota_pending redirect already signals the state to the frontend.

critical_code_review_comments: routes_social.py had a latent NameError (`logger` referenced but not imported) in the gbp_callback failure path — this was silently masked because the code path only fires when accounts.list returns non-200 with a valid access_token. Iteration 18 tests wouldn't have caught it without static grep; suggest a lightweight `python -c 'import routes_social'` smoke test in CI to catch import-time / attribute mistakes.

gbp_status computes `scope_ok` as `"business.manage" in (granted_scopes or "")` — string containment is fine since scopes returned by Google are space-separated full URLs; the substring 'business.manage' will match `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage`. Correct, but a comment would help future readers.
gbp_callback's frontend redirect uses `GBP_REDIRECT_URI.replace('/api/gbp/oauth/callback', ...)` — brittle if the redirect URI ever changes suffix. Consider deriving from FRONTEND_URL env instead.

No unit test simulates the callback path itself (scope missing → 400). The static grep asserts the code exists; a fastapi TestClient test that mocks gbp_exchange_code to return a scope without business.manage would provide behavioural coverage.

rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: OAuth tokens issued before the business.manage scope was added to the Google Cloud consent screen kept working through refresh_token but every accounts.list call returned 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT. Fix in place validates tok['scope'] at the callback (rejects the connection when business.manage missing), probes accounts.list immediately post-exchange and stores its status, exposes the state via /gbp/status (scope_ok, accounts_check_status), and differentiates 403 SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT (reconnect CTA) from other 403 (quota CTA) in gbp_list_locations. Frontend renders a distinct 'Reconnecter (permission manquante)' button when scope_ok===false which disconnects + re-initiates OAuth. Additional latent NameError on `logger` in routes_social.py was fixed in this iteration to prevent a crash in the accounts_check failure branch.
